text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak and Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi acertain the necessity of raising Egyptian-Libyan investments and mutual trade to $1 billion a year. In a final communique, the two leaders say they will try to set up a free zone and also say that it is the right of the Palestinian people to set up their country with Jerusalem as the capital.
- Defence Minister Field Marshal Mohamed Hussein Tantawi will visit Greece and France next week to discuss military cooperation.
- Britain refuses to grant political asylum to Kamal Tawfik Heblawi, the man who runs the European media centre of the terrorist group Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group).
- Egyptians smoke 40 billion cigarettes a year, and this figure will rise to 85 billion from the year 2000.
- World Bank will upgrade its representation in Cairo starting next month.
- Egypt and Libya plant the seed of an Arab common market. Cabinet to hold a special session to look into the idea.
- Libya to invest $200 million in the Toskha project. Egypt sells Libya cloth for 10 million pounds ($2.95 million). There is demand for Egyptian workers in Libya.

- Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid says the government will not tamper with the quantity of subsidised cooking oil and that the state maintains a majority stake in most oil companies. IMF official also says that privatisation will increase incomes.
- Egyptian envoy Osama el-Baz will resume his contacts to save the peace process this week.
- Student impersonates police officer and blackmails people to give him money.
